title: Quantum Computing in Engineering Workflows: Insights from Semiconductor Engineering - News and Statistics
excerpt: Semiconductor Engineering review highlights quantum computing's practical role in graph partitioning for FEA and CFD, plus advances in AMBA AXI5 MPAM verification, solid-state battery simulation, AI trust in automotive, Arm machine-readable specs, standards integration, AI creativity, network-on-chip transport, chiplet data management, cryogenic compact models, and agentic system validation.
content:
Sep 30, 2026

According to a review published by Semiconductor Engineering, Synopsys researcher Prith Banerjee identifies graph partitioning for large finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics simulations as an area where quantum computing already delivers useful applications within broader workflows.

Cadence researcher Divya Bora describes AMBA AXI5 MPAM as a framework for controlling and monitoring shared memory system resources, noting that it introduces a new resource-context correctness challenge to standard AXI protocol verification.

Siemens researcher Anna De Gol examines how simulation can support solid-state battery development through a multi-physics, multi-scale modeling workflow that directly connects battery microstructure to degradation and overall performance.

Keysight researcher Sophie Gerken warns that as machine learning models become increasingly embedded in automotive systems, trust depends on confidence that the artificial intelligence behaves appropriately within its intended context.

Arm researcher Joe McIntyre introduces the Arm Architecture Machine Readable Specification, which offers programmatic access to architecture information in a consistent structure that software can use as a foundation for automating architecture-related tasks.

SEMI researcher Kartikey Srivastava speaks with Daniele Pagano of STMicroelectronics about how integrating standards earlier in the development lifecycle can help bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and commercial deployment.

Technology editor Brian Bailey questions whether artificial intelligence can be creative and asserts that it is impossible to know unless creativity itself is understood, a concept he describes as difficult to articulate.

Arteris researcher Ashley Stevens outlines how to transport native packetized network-on-chip traffic directly across die boundaries using a stable, invariant interface.

Siemens EDA researchers Keith Felton and Todd Burkholder explain why design data management, traceability, and revision control are critical for multi-chiplet heterogeneous integration.

Keysight EDA researcher Fahad Usmani examines the impact of cryogenic temperatures on advanced compact models.

Cadence researcher Vinod Khera digs into how agentic systems make choices, how to ensure they are validated, and who is accountable at final sign-off.
